issues.description: The new FVT13 target omits the execution-termination policy for an intentional spin loop and a consuming queue loop, so the fixed Verus toolchain rejects the target with missing-decreases errors.
issues.rationale: Official Verus 9e262800af8757047b179a36ca655863bc76d005 enforces execution termination checking by default. At the selected FVT13 commit, the verifier reports `loop must have a decreases clause` at both listed loops. The spin loop depends on another participant releasing the lock and needs an explicit `exec_allows_no_decreases_clause` policy; the queue loop pops one page per iteration and supports `decreases pages.len()`. Immediate repair cd964908bc10022ac3f96531dd40ba2af8d40f0c adds those annotations (and a same-root measure to a later `defers` loop), after which the identical target reports 23 verified, 0 errors. This is a verifier-policy rejection, not a claim that the runtime spin loop must terminate.
issues.source_evidence:
after/fvt13-vmspace-unmap-safety/src/spin/exec.rs
201:         while !acquired

after/fvt13-vmspace-unmap-safety/src/tlb/cpu_local_queue/mod.rs
76:         while pages.len() > 0

Pinned problem run reports missing-decreases diagnostics at both locations. Repair cd964908bc10022ac3f96531dd40ba2af8d40f0c adds a function-level exec termination opt-out for the spin lock and `decreases pages.len()` for the consuming queue loop; the repaired target reports `23 verified, 0 errors`.
issues.verification: Independently reproduced twice with Verus 9e262800af8757047b179a36ca655863bc76d005 plus the historical VOSTD compatibility patch, Rust 1.82.0, and Z3 4.12.5: problem snapshot reports two missing-decreases diagnostics; repair snapshot reports 23 verified, 0 errors.
